clauses.clause: sec. 1: no corporation or joint stock company (other than insurance) may do business in the Canal Zone until it files its charter and a verified financial statement with the Collector of Revenues

sec. 2: company must file consent to be sued and appoint the Collector of Revenues and his successors its attorney for service of process, that authority to continue so long as any liability against it remains outstanding in the Canal Zone; no business until filed
sec. 3: on compliance and a $50 annual fee the Collector issues a certificate to do business, terminable by the Chief Executive of the Canal Zone, with proportionate rebate
sec. 4: agent doing business before compliance is liable to a fine up to $25 or jail up to thirty days, each day a separate offense
sec. 5: saving clause; order does not modify the insurance companies order of March 12, 1907
sec. 6: takes effect sixty days after publication in The Canal Record (published April 9, 1913)

propositions.claim: Sec. 1 bars doing business in the Canal Zone until the charter and a verified statement are filed.
propositions.quote: shall do business in the Canal Zone until after it has filed in the office of the Collector of Revenues a duly authenticated copy of its charter

propositions.claim: Sec. 2 requires consent to suit and appointment of the Collector as attorney for service.
propositions.quote: designating the Collector of Revenues, and his successors in office, to be its true and lawful attorney, upon whom all process in any such action may be served

propositions.claim: Sec. 3 provides for a certificate on payment of a $50 annual fee.
propositions.quote: the payment of an annual fee, in advance, of $50, to the Collector of Revenues, he shall issue to such corporation or company a certificate

propositions.claim: Sec. 4 sets the penalty.
propositions.quote: shall be subject to a fine not exceeding $25, or imprisonment in jail not exceeding thirty days

propositions.claim: Sec. 5 saves the 1907 insurance companies order.
propositions.quote: This Order shall not be held to modify the provisions of an Executive Order relating to insurance companies, dated March 12, 1907

propositions.claim: Sec. 6 delays effect sixty days from Canal Record publication (held transcription: 'This Order shall take effect sixty days from the date of its publication in The Canal Record'); the 1922 compilation's footnote gives the publication date, as relayed by the fetch tool from the archive.org OCR at offset 640000 and matched by the held transcription's note 'Published in Canal Record of April 9, 1913.'

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN is appropriate: the confirmed evidence proves neither a qualifying ending nor operation at the cutoff. The missing lifecycle evidence is identified. Formal status is upheld only as the limited report that no express ending was found, not as proof that none exists. General codification and Code repeal cannot establish an unnamed order's ending under the stated rules.
missed_evidence: Held jobs/wikisource-texts/output/texts/EO_1752.txt, section 2, expressly requires service authority to continue 'so long as any liability against it remains outstanding in the Canal Zone.' The clause inventory omits this residual obligation; any eventual closure must address it. No decisive ending was confirmed.
review.stop_code_verdict: wrong (WEB fits): the first gap requires inspecting the named 1934 Code and its source notes. The evidence slice supplies no class-doctrine ruling lead, and the project rules already prohibit inferring an ending from an unnamed general enactment. NEEDS_RULING does not describe the immediate evidence gap.
review.suspected_defect: The original.accepted=true designation conflicts with the acknowledged lack of a held official printing and reliance on a fetch summary. This is an unsupported original qualification; deliberate alteration cannot be determined.

verdicts.reason: The cited Archive.org OCR could not be retrieved through either web access or a direct request. The held transcription confirms identity and date, but cannot confirm the official printing, page, or original acceptance.
Held EO_1752.txt section 1 contains the quoted prohibition and requires the authenticated charter and verified statement.
Held text section 2 expressly requires consent to suit and designation of the Collector and successors for service.
Held text section 3 specifies the annual $50 advance payment and issuance of a certificate; it also confirms termination and conditional rebate.
Held text section 4 confirms the $25 maximum fine or thirty-day maximum imprisonment and separate daily offenses.
Held text section 5 expressly preserves the March 12, 1907 insurance order.
The held transcription corroborates the sixty-day commencement provision and April 9 publication footnote, but the cited official compilation and its footnote could not be checked.

The cited Statutes at Large page confirms the conclusive codification language, with an exception for general United States laws, and does not name EO 1752. It is only a general candidate under the project rules.
The cited govinfo Code note confirms both the 1979 redesignation and the 1996 repeal of the Panama Canal Code; it does not establish a named ending of this order.
The compilation could not be retrieved, so neither the cross-reference quotation nor the claimed absence of repeal or amendment annotations was confirmed.
The cited APP transcription, dated December 19, 1939, expressly revokes EO 2062 in section 4 and contains no reference to corporations or EO 1752. This confirms the limited transcription-based claim.
